detectionTechnologies.name: Visual and stereo microscopy
detectionTechnologies.bestFor: Initial sorting by size, shape and colour
detectionTechnologies.strength: Low-cost screening and useful for larger visible particles.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: It cannot confirm polymer type and is prone to observer bias.

detectionTechnologies.name: FTIR and micro-FTIR spectroscopy
detectionTechnologies.strength: Strong confirmatory method for common polymers and non-destructive analysis.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: Small particles, dark particles, additives and matrix residues can reduce quality.

detectionTechnologies.name: Raman and micro-Raman spectroscopy
detectionTechnologies.bestFor: Polymer identification for small particles and complex shapes
detectionTechnologies.strength: Can analyse smaller particles than many FTIR workflows and gives molecular fingerprints.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: Fluorescence, pigments and sample heating can affect spectra.

detectionTechnologies.name: Py-GC/MS and thermal analysis
detectionTechnologies.strength: Highly useful for complex matrices and polymer mass estimates.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: Destructive method and does not preserve particle count, size or shape information.

detectionTechnologies.name: SEM-EDS
detectionTechnologies.strength: Provides high-resolution imaging and helps identify surface weathering or inorganic interference.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: It is not sufficient as a stand-alone polymer confirmation method.

detectionTechnologies.name: Nile Red fluorescence screening
detectionTechnologies.strength: High-throughput and useful before confirmatory spectroscopy.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: False positives are possible, so confirmation is required.

detectionTechnologies.name: Electrical sensing zone and Coulter-type methods
detectionTechnologies.bestFor: Fast particle counting and size estimation in liquid flow
detectionTechnologies.strength: Suitable for real-time signal-based counting, sizing and automated classification workflows.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: Polymer identity is not directly confirmed unless combined with complementary methods or trained models.

detectionTechnologies.name: AI-assisted imaging and spectral classification
detectionTechnologies.bestFor: Automated sorting, classification and data interpretation
detectionTechnologies.strength: Improves throughput and consistency when trained with strong reference datasets.
detectionTechnologies.limitation: Model reliability depends on representative calibration data and transparent validation.

healthMechanisms.summary: Small particles may interact with tissues depending on size, shape and surface properties. Fibres and fragments can behave differently.
Several experimental studies discuss inflammation and oxidative stress as plausible biological pathways, but human risk thresholds remain uncertain.
Plastic particles may carry additives, residual monomers or environmental pollutants, which can influence toxicological relevance.
Ingestion exposure may interact with the gastrointestinal environment, but the strength of evidence varies by particle type and study design.
Very small microplastics and nanoplastics may have higher potential to cross biological barriers, making them a major research priority.

transformationProcesses: Photo-oxidation caused by sunlight and oxygen
Mechanical fragmentation caused by abrasion, waves and sediment movement
Thermal ageing and polymer chain breakdown
Biofouling and microbial colonisation on particle surfaces
Aggregation with organic matter, minerals or other suspended solids
Leaching of additives and adsorption of external pollutants
Progressive formation of smaller particles, including nanoplastics
researchGaps: Globally harmonised sampling and reporting methods are still limited.
Small microplastics and nanoplastics are difficult to quantify with confidence.
Complex water, wastewater, food and biological matrices create interference.
Field-ready, real-time detection technologies need stronger validation.
Human health evidence is increasing, but dose-response relationships remain uncertain.
Open reference datasets are needed for machine learning based classification.
